text:
Vince Dunn is still the Kraken's offensive defenseman, 22:38 a night, five power-play points and five goals in 23 games, the latest two a drive from the point against Anaheim and another in Edmonton on Friday. Those have pushed his shooting to 10%, above what our talent range expects (closer to 7%), so that part will likely settle.

His own chances are better than last season, 0.44 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.33, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best defensemen at getting to the home-plate area in front of the net. That is the real skill here.

The rest is harder to like. Seattle has only 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, and his ice time has dropped almost two minutes a night over the last ten games. The same tracking flagged his exits: only 31% keep possession, so the forecheck gets the puck back too often. Evolving-Hockey noted his teammates are among the weakest of any defenseman. Watch whether the minutes keep shrinking.
